=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- README.md:178 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In the `FINAL_CI_FAILED_REDISPATCH_ENABLED` row, the sentence "A job cancelled at its `timeout-minutes` limit is still handed back." does not mention the new stale-workflow exception documented in row 180.
  WHY: For an eligible attempt-1 stale-workflow timeout, `scripts/review_final_ci_failed.sh` posts the `ai:final-ci-stale-workflow:v1` marker, logs `outcome=stale_workflow_sync_deferred` and defers to the sweep's base sync instead of handing the job back, so operators reading row 178 get the wrong idea; this is documentation drift only. All three reviewers rated it NIT, which maps to low here; sonnet filed it under NAMING / BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY and luna and glm under CORRECTNESS & LOGIC.
- scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:181 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `STALE_WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE` regex may be brittle because of the non-capturing group `(?:running on runner .+ )?`.
  WHY: If the runner name format changes, the match could fail and cause an unnecessary review hand-back; the source rated it NIT, which maps to low here, and anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash both said it is not a defect because `.+` matches any runner name and a miss falls back to the safe `genuine` hand-back.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- README.md:line 178, the `FINAL_CI_FAILED_REDISPATCH_ENABLED` row, sentence "A job cancelled at its `timeout-minutes` limit is still handed back." | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The PR adds an exception to this sentence, but the row was not updated. `review_final_ci_failed_main` in `scripts/review_final_ci_failed.sh` now posts the `ai:final-ci-stale-workflow:v1` marker and returns `outcome=stale_workflow_sync_deferred` when `review_final_ci_failed_infra_verdict` returns `stale_workflow_timeout`. That happens on attempt 1, in coding-workflows, for a same-repository head outside `orchestrator/project-*`, with base sync on and its cap above 0. Row 180 describes this exception, but row 178 does not.
  WHY: Documentation only. An operator expects a review dispatch for every timeout cancellation, but a timeout under an older `ci.yml` is deferred to the sweep's base sync. The suggested fix is to add "unless the stale-workflow rule applies (see `FINAL_CI_STALE_WORKFLOW_SYNC_ENABLED`)".
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:181 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The `STALE_WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE` regex is brittle because of the non-capturing group `(?:running on runner .+ )?`.
  WHY: If the runner name format changes, or contains characters that interact unexpectedly with `.+`, the regex might not match. That would cause an unnecessary review hand-back instead of identifying a stale-workflow timeout.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- README.md:Line 178, `FINAL_CI_FAILED_REDISPATCH_ENABLED` row, sentence "A job cancelled at its `timeout-minutes` limit is still handed back." | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: This sentence is now false in coding-workflows for the stale-workflow case. Row 180 (`FINAL_CI_STALE_WORKFLOW_SYNC_ENABLED`) and the `stale_workflow_timeout` branch of `review_final_ci_failed_infra_verdict` in `scripts/review_final_ci_failed.sh` show that an eligible attempt-1 job cancelled at its time limit is not handed back. The branch posts the `ai:final-ci-stale-workflow:v1` marker, logs `outcome=stale_workflow_sync_deferred` and defers to the sweep's base sync. The deferral does not depend on `FINAL_CI_FAILED_REDISPATCH_ENABLED`.
  WHY: Documentation drift, not a code failure. An operator or consumer reading row 178 configures or debugs against the wrong behaviour, and the deferral and its fallback path (`stale_workflow=handed_back`) cannot be seen from that row.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
